page: Amazon Web Services m5d.16xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-hypervisor instance equipped with 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores and 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features dedicated CPU resource allocation with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem includes 35 MB of L3 cache alongside support for instruction extensions such as AVX-512F, AES, and FMA. Unlike standard m5 instances, the m5d variant includes 2400 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD local instance storage alongside a 20 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not feature dedicated hardware GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture oriented toward parallel throughput and wide memory pipelines rather than single-threaded processing. In stress-ng and Geekbench testing, single-core CPU metrics fall into the lower quartile, reflected in single-threaded decompression and text processing. In contrast, multi-core metrics scale into the median range, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 44,078.3 and robust AVX performance. Memory subsystem metrics are notably strong, with large-block uncached read bandwidth reaching 189.99 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 91.19 GB/sec. Application testing shows sustained mid-tier performance across Redis operations, PassMark database operations, and static web serving.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the m5d.16xlarge provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio backed by significant high-speed local NVMe scratch storage. This eliminates the necessity of provisioning extra external block storage purely for temporary scratch or cache paths, though local NVMe data is ephemeral. Computational efficiency is maximized under highly threaded parallel workloads that leverage AVX-512 extensions rather than bursty single-threaded tasks.

The Amazon Web Services m5d.16xlarge is suited for multi-tier enterprise applications, distributed caching nodes, batch processing, build and compilation pipelines, and database environments requiring fast local temporary scratch space or buffering.
